CanonicalVars.maps_to: nothing -- the sim passes the literal 1 (stampede.py:70)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new DynamicVar("Power", 1m)` (Stampede.cs:15) is a printed var with no `_`-attribute in `_init_vars`, so `magic_number` returns None where the game prints 1. Contrast card/rage and card/shockwave, which store the same generic `Power` var in `_power_amount`. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed number the sim's `magic_number` cannot surface, so `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card without it. DORMANT for game fidelity, LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<StampedePower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["Power"].BaseValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (Stampede.cs:24) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, StampedePower, 1, applier=ctx.player)`. No animation on either side. StampedePower's end-of-turn auto-play of a random hand Attack is the power stream's -- and it is the same end-of-turn auto-play slot card/howl_from_beyond uses, which the sim maps to `on_player_turn_end`.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `EnergyCost.UpgradeBy(-1)` (Stampede.cs:29) == `self._energy_cost = max(0, self._energy_cost - 1)` (2 -> 1). The Power var stays 1 when upgraded on both sides.
